run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T01:27:39Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy matches a real, observed burst of ERROR-status spans on frontend-proxy's `ingress` and `router frontend egress` spans between roughly 01:19 and 01:24 UTC (error ratio up to 0.0253 versus a 0.00018-0.00094 baseline earlier in the same window), and the proxy's own access log records those failures as `POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream`. The failing path was followed one step down at a time: frontend's `POST /api/checkout`, `POST`, `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout` and `grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` spans, and checkout's `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` and `oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge` spans, all carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the same minutes, while other otel-demo services stayed at background error levels. The one change observed on that dependency is a restart of the single-replica `payment` Deployment at 01:18:01Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786, old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 stopped at 01:18:04Z) with identical image, environment and resources; the first proxy HTTP 500 appears about 50 seconds later. Payment itself shows no failure evidence: its own ERROR-status span series is identically 0 in that period and its pod logs show every charge it received completing, so calls that reached payment succeeded while about 18% of checkout's Charge client spans failed - consistent with client-side connection failures after the pod was replaced, though that intermediate mechanism is not directly observed. Because incident-time traces are absent from Jaeger (newest trace 01:13:31) and the alerting rule is not loaded in this Prometheus (the reported 0.0222 could not be reproduced), the causal link is the best-supported hypothesis rather than a fully closed chain.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's ERROR-status span ratio rose from 0.00018-0.00094 over 01:03:39-01:18:39 to 0.0108 at 01:19:39, 0.0253 at 01:20:39, 0.0255 at 01:21:39, 0.0252 at 01:22:39 and 0.0149 at 01:23:39, then returned to 0.00073 at 01:24:39 and stayed near 0.0007 through 01:37:39.

frontend-proxy's error ratio is confined to two operations: span_name="ingress" (peak 0.0255) and span_name="router frontend egress" (0.0108-0.0253 during the burst, exactly 0 before 01:19:39 and from 01:24:39 onward, while `ingress` retained a small non-zero background afterwards). These two span names are the only frontend-proxy operations the metric reports.

frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks logged 55 access-log lines containing an HTTP 500 in 01:18:30-01:24:00, every one of them `POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream` (earliest shown 01:18:53.430Z, latest shown 01:19:48.874Z before the returned-limit cut), while surrounding checkout traffic on the same log was `POST /api/checkout ... 200 - via_upstream`.

In the same window the checkout service's own spans errored: span_name="oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" and span_name="oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.1802/s and 0.1584/s at 01:20:00, 0.1534/s and 0.1488/s at 01:22:00, 0.1519/s and 0.1519/s at 01:24:00, and exactly 0 from 01:25:00 onward.

Over 01:18:30-01:25:00 the checkout service's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge recorded 44.42 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans against 208 non-error spans, while over the narrower 01:20:00-01:25:00 range the same series shows 0 error and 213.33 non-error.

The frontend service's own error spans in those minutes are exactly the checkout path: span_name="POST /api/checkout", "POST", "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" and "grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" each at 0.2556/s errors at 01:20:00, decaying to 0.1519/s at 01:23:00 and 0 from 01:24:00; frontend's "/api/cart", "/api/data" and "grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart" spans show 0 errors throughout.

The `payment` Deployment was restarted at 01:18:01Z: its current ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 was created 2026-11-17T01:18:01Z with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:18:01Z, while the previous ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 (created 2026-11-17T00:45:49Z) is scaled to 0; both templates carry the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, the same env (PAYMENT_PORT 8080, FLAGD_HOST flagd, FLAGD_PORT 8013, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT http://$(OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME):4317) and the same limits (cpu 20m, memory 160Mi), so this is a restart rather than a configuration change.

otel-demo events record the payment rollout: Deployment/payment ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled up replica set payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1" at 01:18:01Z, ReplicaSet/payment-54499f9786 SuccessfulCreate pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d, Pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d Started container payment at 01:18:04Z, and Pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 Killing "Stopping container payment" at 01:18:04Z with ReplicaSet/payment-55766d76b9 SuccessfulDelete and Deployment/payment scale-down 1 to 0.

The only payment pod now, payment-54499f9786-4r25d, is Running, Ready=true, owned by ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786, started 2026-11-17T01:18:01Z with restartCount 0, and the payment Deployment reports readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1, updatedReplicas=1, replicas=1; all other otel-demo pods started 00:45:48-00:47:43Z with restartCount 0.

The payment service itself shows no failure during the burst: pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d logged 95 lines in 01:20:00-01:21:00 pairing "Charge request received." with "Transaction complete." for every charge, and 68 such lines in 01:26:00-01:27:00, with no error text; its traces_span_metrics_calls_total carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 at every point from 01:20:00 to 01:38:00 (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET is non-zero) and its own `charge` span series has UNSET 160.01 over 390s with no ERROR series at all - so calls that reached payment were served successfully even while checkout's client spans failed.

checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp logged 51 successful "payment went through" lines in 01:18:30-01:21:00 (newest shown 01:20:54-01:20:59), i.e. many orders succeeded in the same minutes that contain the failed Charge client spans and the proxy HTTP 500s.

Outside the checkout path, service error levels were background only: ad, fraud-detection and recommendation each show isolated 0.0037/s points (about one error per 5-minute window) that also appear before the burst, payment is 0 throughout, and cart, currency, shipping, email and product-catalog show 0 for the returned series in 01:20-01:38.

The otel-demo NetworkPolicy query returned an empty object list, and the otel-demo Services are ordinary ClusterIP services (frontend-proxy 100.64.42.83:8080, frontend 100.68.43.111:8080, checkout 100.70.91.46:8080, flagd 100.66.245.109 on 8013/8016/4000).

The flagd-config ConfigMap currently declares, for payment, paymentUnreachable defaultVariant "on" ("Payment service is unavailable") and paymentFailure defaultVariant "off" (variants off=0, 10%=0.1, 25%=0.25, 50%=0.5, 75%=0.75, 90%=0.95, 100%=1), with every other flag in the file defaulting to "off"; the payment service's own span names include "charge" and "grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveFloat", i.e. it evaluates a numeric flag.

The frontend-proxy spans still available from Jaeger (window 01:13:25.935-01:13:31.667Z) carry only http.status_code 200 and 308 with no error details, and their only visible parent-child links are `router frontend egress` as CHILD_OF `ingress`; the sampled view contains no error spans and no spans after 01:13:31.667Z.

Best-supported causal chain: the Deployment/payment restart at 01:18:01Z removed the only payment pod (stopped 01:18:04Z); for roughly five minutes checkout's Charge calls failed while the new pod served the calls that reached it, producing STATUS_CODE_ERROR on checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans and on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder; the frontend /api/checkout handler then returned HTTP 500, which frontend-proxy recorded as 500 - via_upstream on its `ingress` and `router frontend egress` spans, driving the RequestErrorRate alert for frontend-proxy. The mechanism linking the pod replacement to the failed client calls is inferred from timing and from payment's clean logs, not directly observed.

Rejected as the cause of this burst: the fault-injection flag paymentUnreachable="on" in flagd-config declaring the payment service unavailable. That would fail every charge, yet payment completed every charge it received in 01:20:00-01:21:00 and checkout logged 51 "payment went through" successes in 01:18:30-01:21:00, the error burst ended while the ConfigMap still reads "on", and payment's own ERROR-status series stayed 0.

Rejected as the cause of this burst: a percentage paymentFailure injection active inside payment. paymentFailure's current defaultVariant is "off", and in 01:20:00-01:21:00 the payment pod logged 47 "Charge request received." lines each followed by "Transaction complete." with no failed charge, which a 25% in-service failure would contradict; payment's own span series carries no ERROR status at all.

The alert's reported current value 0.0222 at 01:27:39Z is best explained as the 01:19-01:24 error burst retained in the alert's evaluation window: the ratios computable at that instant are 0.01159 (10m, all frontend-proxy spans), 0.00566 (20m), 0.00382 (30m) and 0.01192 (10m, ingress only), and the burst peak ratios were 0.0253 all-span and 0.0255 ingress-only, so the exact rule window cannot be confirmed from the available data.

Recommend obtaining the RequestErrorRate rule expression, threshold and evaluation window from the Alertmanager/Prometheus that actually evaluates it, since this target exposes no alerting or recording rules, so that the reported 0.0222 value and the 01:27:39Z start can be tied to a specific window.

Recommend reviewing why the single-replica Deployment payment was restarted at 01:18:01Z and checking client-side gRPC connection convergence after pod replacement for single-replica dependencies (draining connections, more replicas, or verifying readiness before the old pod is removed) instead of treating the restart itself as the fault.

gaps: Jaeger's newest trace is 01:13:31.667Z, before the 01:18-01:24 failure window: a traces_search for service frontend-proxy over 01:15:00-01:44:10 (evidence 2f67a1e1-0835-4ece-b423-5ebb61131e69-t1:3802af34-3c55-4751-96b4-b3d29a9d8e7e) returned nothing, so the burst's span status tags, error details and parent-child edges for the failing Charge/PlaceOrder/checkout calls are unknown.

A list_prometheus_rules query by rule_name=RequestErrorRate and a second by type=alert both returned nothing (evidence 418b4ff3-9bdc-48fe-a9dc-fc4bd6b7860d-t0:db6c847d-61eb-4786-ac96-a4fe9959072f and 3abdb984-ebec-44d4-8ea6-8f4e2c51bb5b-t0:09d470aa-12f6-4efb-846f-c16a844614ae, both status no_data), so the alerting rule's expression, threshold and window are unknown and the annotation value 0.0222 could not be reproduced.

A 5-minute-window error-ratio query at 01:27:39Z over all frontend-proxy spans returned nothing (27c97d09-240e-4c2b-943b-8097db740192-t1:3b74388a-92af-4ca0-b8f3-0a54c56302e3, status no_data), so the 5m reading at the alert start is unknown rather than zero.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what issued the payment rollout restart at 01:18:01Z (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) and whether flagd flag values differed during 01:18-01:24 cannot be verified; the flagd-config ConfigMap only shows current values.

A filtered search for "error" in checkout pod logs over 01:18:30-01:21:00 returned nothing (b56c58ff-d60e-49c3-a135-6e9c97424c1e-t1:f2583486-3efd-4baf-a971-31f47db5583b, status no_data), so checkout's failure text for the failed Charge calls was not observed.

The frontend pod's logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt over 01:19:00-01:22:30 returned 0 lines (841b3c44-9bb0-4019-977e-d2ab94fb1184-t1:7f08919e-d41e-413c-b8a4-bd48d83d6158, status no_data), so the frontend-side message behind the proxy HTTP 500s is unknown.
The deleted payment pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 has no readable current or previous instance, so its shutdown behaviour and its view of the transition are unknown.

A filtered search for " 500 " in frontend-proxy logs over 01:20:00-01:25:30 returned nothing (2b297a11-c73f-488a-848c-5f5d60d3e61c-t0:684b5dad-dfa2-48d3-bce4-85ac23cdcc3e, status no_data) while span metrics show frontend-proxy errors continuing to about 01:23:39, so the exact end time of the HTTP 500s is unresolved; the returned 500 lines are also limited to the newest 40 of 55 matches.

The concrete mechanism linking the payment pod replacement to checkout's failed Charge calls (for example stale gRPC connections or conntrack entries to the deleted pod IP) is inferred from timing and from payment's clean logs, not directly observed.

No ResourceQuota objects matched the query for namespace otel-demo (bac38135-69c2-4652-a022-e90b9a355ee7-t2:c82f43fb-d39f-4f60-a8d0-be3f6f7eada7, status no_data), and other quota sources were not examined, so quota pressure is not fully excluded.

A filtered search for error text in the new payment pod over 01:15:00-01:30:00 returned nothing (284c5341-f60d-4b57-9d0a-01a676f2fbdd-t2:8d74fdd4-e59a-48d4-9bda-a9ee64062f2e, status no_data) and the previous payment container does not exist, so any payment-side error output during the transition is unknown.
next_steps: Obtain the RequestErrorRate rule definition and the alert's full history (startsAt, value timeline) from the Prometheus/Alertmanager that evaluates it, to confirm which window carried the 0.0222 reading.
Review the audit/change log for Deployment/payment around 2026-11-17T01:18:01Z to identify who ran the rollout restart and whether any flagd flag value changed around 01:18-01:24.
Capture full distributed traces (or restore trace export) for the 01:18-01:25 window so the failing Charge calls' status codes and error details can be read rather than inferred.
Verify post-restart client behaviour of checkout's gRPC channel to the payment ClusterIP (retry/backoff and connection re-resolution settings) to confirm or rule out the stale-connection hypothesis.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

notes: Container frontend-proxy has no previous instance (HTTP 400: previous terminated container "frontend-proxy" in pod "frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks" not found); the other streams are unaffected.
5584 lines outside the query window were dropped (0 before its start, 5584 after its end).
